subject: Dedicated capacity: staircase commit, burst credits, and model-mix sizing
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle@crestline.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@crestline.ai
Date: 2026-08-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial workload export attached

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is the CSV export of our production workload (crestline_workload_v1.csv) — per-minute request counts for the last 30 days plus sample context lengths. Key points: average request size ~420 tokens (prompt + completion), 95th pct concurrency ~340 concurrent active sessions during peak, and sustained request rate ~220 reqs/sec for a 60-minute window during business hours.

Primary ask: we want a pricing proposal for a reserved commit that ensures 99.95% availability at sub-300ms median latency for our lightweight model (7B) and a fallback SLA for heavier 70B models during planned batch windows. We're also interested in burst credits for predictable seasonal spikes and a tiered discount tied to a 12-month commit.

Can you sketch the sizing assumptions you would use and a sample commit/discount structure? We're aiming to finalize a packaging option for our Q4 budget.

Thanks — Janelle
CTO, Crestline Systems
--
Janelle Park

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle@crestline.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-05T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial workload export attached

Hi Janelle — thanks for the export, that was very helpful. Quick read and some clarifying Qs below before we lock numbers:

- Confirmed: average request ~420 tokens, 95p concurrency ~340, sustained peak ~220 rps.
- Which model mix is the primary production path? You mentioned "lightweight 7B" for most traffic and "70B" for scheduled analytic jobs — what percent of tokens do you expect to route to 70B versus 7B (estimates OK)?
- Do you require guaranteed median latency <300ms across both models, or just for 7B with a higher latency tolerance for 70B?

Preliminary sizing assumptions (high level):
- Model mix assumption: 90% 7B, 10% 70B (adjustable).
- Effective tokens/sec calculation: 220 reqs/sec * 420 tokens = 92,400 tokens/sec total. Assuming 90% on 7B => 83,160 tokens/sec on 7B workload.
- Serving profile: with our latency-optimized execution path and 8-bit quantization for the 7B model, one A100-class GPU can sustain roughly 9k-12k tokens/sec at p50 ~120-180ms (varies by prompt/response length). For 70B (quantized + KV cache), one GPU covers ~1.5k-2.5k tokens/sec at p50 ~350-500ms.

Sizing sketch (baseline):
- Baseline pool for 7B: 83,160 tokens/sec / 10,500 tokens/sec per GPU ~= 8 GPUs (round up to 8).
- 70B capacity for scheduled jobs: 9 GPUs to cover occasional bursts (we recommend reserving 2-3 GPUs dedicated to 70B or using canary routing to shared pool depending on isolation needs).
- Nominal recommendation: start with a 12-GPU pool (balanced across model variants) + a 20% burst credit buffer (equivalent to ~2-3 GPU-hours/day of headroom translated into monthly credits).

Pricing / commit structure (initial):
- 12-GPU reserved commit, 12-month term: base list = $72,000/mo (example list pricing).
- Tiered discount schedule: 10% off at 6-month prepay, 18% off at 12-month prepay, additional 3% rebate tied to telemetry-based efficiency gains if average batch utilization exceeds 65% for two consecutive months.
- Burst credits: include 150 GPU-hours/month of burst credit (non-committed) with overage billed at on-demand rate; unused credits do not roll over.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime, with automatic fallback routing to hosted pool (subject to capacity) for catastrophic failures; p50 latency guarantees apply to 7B only.

I'll loop Ben for the commercial packaging and Priyom for a quick run of the exact tokens/sec -> GPU mapping using your CSV. If you're open, we can also propose a staircase commit (lower guaranteed baseline for months 1-3 with increasing guaranteed GPU count month-over-month) to better match your expected ramp.

Next steps: Ben will draft a numeric pricing doc + optional staircase commit scenarios; Priyom will run a runbook that maps your per-minute trace to simulated GPU utilization and return a recommended pool size with 95% confidence. Can we target EOD Friday for that pack?

Best,
Stephanie
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle@crestline.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-06T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — staircase commit options and commercials

Hi Janelle — following up with concrete commercial options (rounded numbers to keep the note concise). I attached a draft proposal PDF (redwood_proposal_draft.pdf). Summary: 

Option A — Flat reserved (simplest)
- 12 GPUs reserved (mix: 9x for 7B, 3x for 70B), 12-month term
- Price: $61,200/mo (15% discount applied to list)
- Burst credits: 150 GPU-hours/mo included; overage $18/hr
- Overage protection: 10% headroom automated; excess routed to on-demand at capped rate of $25/hr

Option B — Staircase ramp (recommended if you expect phased rollout)
- Months 1-3: guarantee 8 GPUs (saves cash in ramp), months 4-12: guarantee 12 GPUs
- Effective blended price: $54,900/mo equivalent (18% weighted discount)
- Burst credits: 200 GPU-hours/mo for first 3 months, then 150/mo afterward
- Early-termination: prorated based on realized utilization vs committed baseline

Option C — High-commit anchor (best unit economics)
- 16 GPUs reserved, 12-month prepaid
- Price: $76,800/mo (25% discount on list for higher commit)
- Burst credits: 300 GPU-hours/mo + 5% telemetry rebate if utilization >70%

Notes on guarantees and model-mix:
- We can apply the p50 <300ms guarantee for 7B if you accept a soft SLA for 70B (we measure and alert but don't offer strict p50 for the large model).
- For mixed routing we provision GPU counts conservatively; Priyom's utilization run will give more confidence.

Commercial asks from Crestline:
- If procurement requires invoice-level net-60, that will change discount thresholds (Ben to coordinate).
- If you want dedicated disks/HSM for audit, that increases the platform fee by a fixed $1,200/mo.

If this package looks reasonable I can convert Option B into a formal quote with line-item pricing and contract terms. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through.

Thanks — Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Janelle Park <janelle@crestline.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@crestline.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-07T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — staircase commit options and commercials

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear options. A few clarifications before we proceed: 

1) Staircase looks attractive — can you confirm the exact metric used for "guarantee" each month (is it guaranteed GPU-hours or guaranteed average concurrent GPUs)? We need the commitment expressed as a monthly guaranteed GPU-hours for our procurement team.
2) For Option B, would the first 3 months' higher burst credit (200 GPU-hrs) be additive to the baseline or replace it? We prefer additive.
3) If we accept the staircase, can you insert a clause that allows us one-time annual re-evaluation to downsize if utilization consistently <55% for four consecutive months?

Assuming we can get the above items codified, Procurement will push for net-45 payment terms; can you surface how that impacts the discount?

Once we have the clarified quote, we'll circulate internally and aim to sign by Aug 21 to hit our Q4 rollout schedule. Thank you — Janelle
CTO, Crestline Systems
